note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 67; A06b Const 67; L05 Const 70(1)(a)-(d), PNG 6C): ordinary naturalisation after 8 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Papua New Guinea, 2024
sources.said: Residence for 8 years required. ... Renunciation of foreign citizenship required (except if person is a citizen of a prescribed country and obtained permission for retention of citizenship). ... Automatic loss of citizenship by obtaining nationality or citizenship of another country by voluntary act other than marriage. Automatic loss of citizenship by exercising a right exclusive to nationals of another country or taking oath or allegiance to foreign country. Except if citizenship of a designated country is acquired and permission is requested for retention of citizenship (Australia, Fiji, Germany, New Zealand, Samoa, United Kingdom, United States of America and Vanuatu). Automatic loss of citizenship where person travels on a foreign passport (some exceptions, including with approval of minister).
